title: PUCN Order — Docket 26-04026 (2026-07-10)

Application of SV RNO Property Owner 1 LLC, under
the provisions of the Utility Environmental Protection

temporary 144 MW natural gas-fueled electric
generating facility and associated facilities to be located
on private land in Storey County, Nevada.

Application of PR RNO Property Owner 1, LLC, under
the provisions of the Utility Environmental Protection
Act, for a permit to construct the Peru Ridge Self-
Generation Project consisting of a temporary 218 MW
natural gas-fueled electric generating facility and
associated facilities to be located on private land in
Storey County, Nevada.

Docket No. 26-04027

NTS SSS OS SS OS OOS OS OS

PROCEDURAL ORDER NO. 2

The presiding officer in this docket makes the following findings and conclusions:

1. On April 20, 2026, SV RNO Property Owner 1 LLC (“SV RNO”), filed with the
Public Utilities Commission of Nevada (“Commission”) an application, designated as Docket
No. 26-04026, under the provisions of the Utility Environmental Protection Act, for a permit to
construct the South Valley Temporary Power Generation Facility consisting of a temporary 144
megawatt natural gas-fueled electric generating facility and associated facilities to be located on
private land in Storey County, Nevada. SV RNO filed the application pursuant to the Nevada
Revised Statutes (“NRS”) and the Nevada Administrative Code (“NAC”), Chapters 703 and 704,
including, but not limited to, NRS 704.820 through 704.900 and NAC 703.415 through 703.427.

2. On April 24, 2026, the Commission issued a Notice of Application for Utility
Environmental Protection Act Permit to Construct a Utility Facility in Docket No. 26-04026 and

SV RNO filed an amendment to the application.

Docket Nos. 26-04026 and 26-04027 Page 2

3. On April 20, 2026, PR RNO Property Owner 1, LLC (“PR RNO” and jointly with
SV RNO, the “Applicant”) filed with the Commission an application, designated as Docket No.
26-04027, under the provisions of the Utility Environmental Protection Act, for a permit to
construct the Peru Ridge Self-Generation Project consisting of a temporary 218 megawatt natural
gas fueled electric generating facility and associated facilities to be located on private land in
Storey County, Nevada. PR RNO filed the application pursuant to the NRS and the NAC,
Chapters 703 and 704, including, but not limited to, NRS 704.820 through 704.900 and NAC
703.415 through 703.427.

4. On April 24, 2026, the Commission issued a Notice of Application for Utility
Environmental Protection Act Permit to Construct a Utility Facility in Docket No. 26-04027 and
PR RNO filed an amendment to the application.

5. The Regulatory Operations Staff of the Commission (“Staff”) participates as a
matter of right pursuant to NRS 703.301.

6. On May 20, 2026, Nevadans for Clean Affordable Reliable Energy (“NCARE”)
filed notices of intent to be a party in both Docket Nos. 26-04026 and 26-04027.

7. On May 22, 2026, the Commission issued a Notice of Prehearing Conference in

Docket No. 26-04026.

8. On May 28, 2026, the Commission issued a Notice of Prehearing Conference in
Docket No. 26-04027.

9. On June 8, 2026, Applicant filed motions to dispense with the hearing in both
Docket Nos. 26-04026 and 26-04027 (“Applicant Motions”).

10. On/June 12, 2026, NCARE filed responses in opposition to the motions in both

Docket Nos. 26-04026 and 26-04027 (“NCARE Opposition”).

Docket Nos. 26-04026 and 26-04027 Page 3

11. OnJune 15, 2026, Staff filed letters indicating it was not taking a position on the
pending motions in both Docket Nos. 26-04026 and 26-04027. On the same day, the presiding
officer held a prehearing conference in Docket No. 26-04026, attended by the Applicant, Staff
and NCARE, wherein consolidation, the pending motion and a procedural schedule were
discussed. No party objected to consolidation.

12. On/June 16, 2026, the presiding officer held a prehearing conference in Docket
No. 26-04027, attended by the Applicant, Staff and NCARE, wherein consolidation, the pending
motion and a procedural schedule were discussed. No party objected to consolidation.

13. On June 17, 2026, the Commission issued Procedural Order No. 1, consolidating
Docket Nos. 26-04026 and 26-04027 for hearing purposes and setting a procedural schedule.

14. On June 22, 2026, the Applicant filed prepared direct testimony, and a reply to the
NCARE Opposition (“Applicant Reply”).

15. On July 1, 2026, the Commission issued a Notice of Hearing.

A, Motion
Applicant’s Position!

16. Applicant states that NRS 704.880 reflects a legislative judgment that an
uncontested application for a permit to construct can be decided without a hearing, providing that
“[t]he Commission, in its discretion, may dispense with the hearing on the application if, upon
the expiration of the time fixed in the notice thereof, no protest against the granting of the permit
has been filed by or in behalf of any interested party.” (Applicant Motions at 2.)

17. Applicant states that the time fixed in the Commission’s notice has expired, and

| As the Applicant Motions filed in Docket Nos. 26-04026 and 26-04027 are almost identical, and the NCARE
Opposition and Applicant Reply are identical, the Commission, herein, will refer to the motion originally filed in
Docket No. 24-04026 for citation purposes.

Docket Nos. 26-04026 and 26-04027 Page 4

no protest against the granting of the permit has been filed, as Applicant contends that NCARE’s
notice of intent to intervene does not count as a protest. (/d.)

18. Applicant states that a notice of intent confers party status but does not register
opposition to the granting of the permit and is not a protest. Applicant further states that NRS
704.880 conditions the Commission’s discretion on whether a protest has been filed, not on
whether the docket has acquired parties. Applicant states that, should NCARE wish to be heard,
it may file a statement of its position and participate in the Commission’s consideration of the
written record without an evidentiary hearing. (/d. at 3.)

19. Applicant further states that the applications satisfy every UEPA filing, notice,
and service requirement, and that no disputed issue of material fact requires a hearing. Applicant
contends that the broader policy debate about data center load and behind-the-meter generation is
not before the Commission in these Dockets. (/d. at 3-5.)

NCARE Opposition

20. NCARE states that it is a proper party to the contested permit proceedings in the
above-captioned dockets pursuant to the Nevada Administrative Procedures Act (“APA”), which
governs and provides the minimum procedural requirements for adjudicatory proceedings before
state executive agencies. NCARE further states that, as a party to these contested cases, it has
the right to present relevant evidence and to examine and cross-examine witnesses at a hearing.
(NCARE Opposition at 3.)

21. NCARE states that Applicant’s position is incorrect and elevates form over
substance, contrary to the plain meaning of NRS 704.880. NCARE further states that, if
adopted, Applicant’s position would violate the minimum procedural requirements governing

adjudicatory proceedings before state executive agencies. NCARE states that the evidentiary

Docket Nos. 26-04026 and 26-04027 Page 5

process in this case is not concluded but is only beginning, and that it will actively pursue its
interests in this matter. (/d.)

22. NCARE asserts it has a right to hearings in both dockets, as the APA provides
that “[i]n a contested case, all parties must be afforded an opportunity for hearing after
reasonable notice,” and that an “[o]pportunity must be afforded all parties to respond and present
evidence and argument on all issues involved.” (/d. at 5, citing NRS 233B.121.)

23. | NCARE states that it opposes the applications as filed and will address the
required findings the Commission must make under NRS 704.890(1), and will examine and
cross-examine witnesses at hearing. (/d. at 12-13.)

Applicant’s Reply Position

24. Applicant states that UEPA establishes a distinct and streamlined statutory
framework, reflecting a legislative intent to resolve permit applications efficiently upon Staff and
Commission review of a completed application, consistent with statutory and regulatory
requirements and without unnecessary duplication. Applicant further states that the plain
language of NRS 704.880 vests the Commission with broad discretion to dispense with a hearing
absent the filing of a qualifying protest, and that NCARE’s filings do not satisfy that statutory
standard. Applicant states that, even if the Commission were to look beyond the threshold
statutory issue, NCARE has not identified any specific, material dispute of fact that would
necessitate an evidentiary hearing, particularly in light of the Legislature’s directive that prior
environmental findings be incorporated rather than re-litigated. (Applicant Reply at 2.)

25. Applicant states that NCARE’s Notice of Intent does not set forth substantive
objections to the application, identify disputed issues of material fact, or request that the

Commission deny or condition the permit in any particular manner, and it, therefore, cannot

Docket Nos. 26-04026 and 26-04027 Page 6

reasonably be construed as a protest within the meaning of NRS 704.880. (/d. at 5.)

26. Applicant states that the purpose of an evidentiary hearing is to resolve disputed
issues of fact that cannot otherwise be adequately evaluated. Applicant further states that, where
no such disputes are identified, a hearing serves little purpose other than to delay the proceeding
and impose additional burdens on the parties and the Commission. (/d. at 6.)

27. Applicant states that NCARE may present its position on the pending application
through a briefing memorandum, just as Staff does. Applicant further states that this procedure
allows NCARE to convey its views to the Commission without the need for evidentiary
submissions or live testimony, and confirms that dispensing with a hearing leaves NCARE with
a full and adequate opportunity to participate. (/d. at 7.)

Commission Discussion and Findings

28. Applicant bases its motions on the assertion that, because NCARE’s Notice of
Intent to Intervene did not use the word “protest,” it does not create a controversy requiring a
hearing.

29. The record does not support the conclusion that NCARE intervened for any
purpose other than to oppose the applications. Elevating the absence of the word “protest” over
the substance of NCARE’s participation would deprive a party of the opportunity to present
evidence at hearing, and the Commission declines to do so.

30. Although the motions are framed as a means of promoting administrative
efficiency, requiring the parties and the Commission to address them has produced the opposite
result.

31. | The Commission finds that NCARE’s Notice of Intent to Intervene is akin to a

protest, and, pursuant to NAC 703.530, construes it as such.
